newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares gain on hopes of Dadas earnings.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares gain on hopes of Dadas earnings.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.71 percent on Monday and market participants said further gains were on the cards due to hopes of good earnings from market heavyweight Dadas, a financial consultancy.
"Dadas claims it'll be in profit despite the problems it faced this year. If its results confirm this, then the index could rise above 1,000 short-term," said Toni Apollonio, an analyst at A banka.
A Dadas spokesman said the company would release 1995 results by the end of this week.

Dadas started facing serious problems at the end of March, when the Securities Market Agency moved to prohibit Dadas' mutual fund Proficia Dadas from trading, claiming the fund was involved in irregular trading practices.
Since then, Dadas shares have plunged over 85 percent, sending the SBI index down 33 percent.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 7.09 points to 988,35.
* Seven shares rose and six fell, while 10 were untraded.
* Turnover slumped to 28.1 million tolars from 52.3 million on Friday.
* Dadas had the highest turnover, rising 4.54 percent to 35,481 tolars on volume of 381 shares for total turnover of 13.5 million tolars.
* Pharmaceutical company Salus was the top gainer, surging 9.91 percent to 9,550 on volume of 50 shares for total turnover of 0.5 million tolars.

* Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the leading decliners, falling 3.77 percent to 10,200 on volume of 51 shares for total turnover of 0.5 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
